newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee firm on slack dollar demand.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee firm on slack dollar demand.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee was firm against the dollar in early Tuesday trade due to slack demand for the greenback, dealers said.
The rupee was at 56.98 to the dollar at 0445 GMT, after opening at 57.07. The rupee closed at 57.03 on Monday.
"The rupee opened down due to overseas gains by the dollar, but there was no local demand to support the dollar," said a Union Bank dealer.
But dealers said there could be late import covering demand for dollars, which could support the currency later in the day.
"But I still do not see the dollar rising to over about 57.10 to the rupee," said the Union Bank dealer.
Last week's Central Bank decision to allow exporters to borrow foreign currency was having a calming effect, he said.
Overnight call money was at 13.75 percent.
"Low call rates, although a big state borrower is in the market, are also a sign that a relaxed monetary policy is having an impact," said an American Express Bank dealer.
The Central Bank also relaxed the statutory reserve requirement last week. "Usually the mere fact that a state bank is in the market drives rates crazy", he said.
